proofs.proof_tex:
The upper inequality is exactly the operational consequence of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:honest\text{-}upper\text{-}frontier}\).  That theorem constructs one schedule-independent kernel \(K^\star\in\mathcal C_\alpha\) and proves
\[
 \sup_{Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,\Gamma}}
 \mathbb E^{K^\star}_{\mathcal D,Y}
 [\operatorname{len}(I^\star)]
 \le2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(K\in\mathcal C_\alpha\), exactly as prescribed by Definition \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}minimax\text{-}length}\), gives
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\le2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]

For the unconditional lower inequality, \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) implies
\[
 \eta_\alpha=\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}
 \in(0,1-2\alpha).
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:mixture\text{-}modulus\text{-}length\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\), applied at this value, therefore gives
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \ge\eta_\alpha
 \Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha).
\]
Both inequalities hold for every design and fixed-schedule class satisfying the primitive assumptions.

Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:rare\text{-}history\text{-}alpha\text{-}only\text{-}obstruction}\) constructs admissible designs for which
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\longrightarrow0.
\]
If a positive \(c_\alpha\), depending only on \(\alpha\), satisfied \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) uniformly over the primitive class, division by the positive quantity \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\) would give \(c_\alpha\le\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\) for every \(n\), contradicting the displayed limit.  This proves the generic obstruction.

Now impose the stated masked-history reachability condition.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:masked\text{-}focal\text{-}modulus\text{-}certificate}\), with \(\gamma=\Gamma\), gives
\[
 \Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\ge2M w(S).
\]
Combining this with the already proved mixture-modulus lower bound yields
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge2\eta_\alpha M w(S).
\]
The structural weight condition \(2M w(S)\ge\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\), together with \(\eta_\alpha>0\), therefore implies
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \ge2\eta_\alpha M w(S)
 \ge\eta_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
Together with the universal factor-two upper bound, this is the claimed restricted-class equivalence.  The masked-modulus lemma derives its testing pair from the finite adaptive tree; no radius-to-modulus comparison is assumed.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and \(M>0\).  There is a sequence of admissible three-block adaptive platform designs \(\mathcal D_n\), each having \(B=3\), \(W=\{2\}\), \(\Gamma=0\), and a strictly positive propensity floor \(p_{\min,n}\), such that
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M,
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star}
      {\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently, over the primitive adaptive-design class there is no constant \(c_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) for which \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) holds uniformly.  The obstruction is a low-propensity history of probability below the permitted miscoverage level, not a failure of positivity in any member of the sequence.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 \varepsilon=\frac{\alpha}{2},
 \qquad
 \delta_n=\frac{\varepsilon}{n}.
\]
For every sufficiently large integer \(n\), take \(B=3\), \(W=\{2\}\), \(q_2=1\), and \((n_1,n_2,n_3)=(1,n,1)\).  Add an arm label \(a\notin\{z_0,z_1\}\) and set
\[
 A_1=\{z_0,a\},\qquad
 A_2=\{z_0,z_1\},\qquad
 A_3=\{z_0\}.
\]
At the only position in block \(1\), assign \(a\) with probability \(\varepsilon\) and \(z_0\) with probability \(1-\varepsilon\).  Define the predictable event
\[
 E=\{Z_{11}=a\}.
\]
Thus \(E\) is known before block \(2\), and \(P^O_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(E)=\varepsilon\) for every fixed schedule \(Y\).  At every position in block \(2\), set
\[
 p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i})=
 \begin{cases}
  \delta_n,&E,\\
  1/2,&E^c,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 p_{2i}(z_0\mid H_{2i})=1-p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i}),
\]
and assign \(z_0\) with probability one in block \(3\).  The probabilities are measurable with respect to the pre-assignment histories, so Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization}\) holds by construction.  Their support is exactly the displayed availability set.  For all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 0<\delta_n\le
 \min\{\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon,1/2,1-\delta_n\},
\]
so Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:availability\text{-}support}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:propensity\text{-}floor}\) hold with \(p_{\min,n}=\delta_n>0\).  The availability-window assumption also holds.  At \(\Gamma=0\), the schedule class consists of bounded fixed potential-outcome arrays whose three control block means are equal, so the boundedness and control-total-variation assumptions remain in force.

We first evaluate the frozen optimized radius.  Definition \(\mathrm{def:concurrent\text{-}weights}\) gives \(u_2=1\).  The focal-arm summand in Definition \(\mathrm{def:average\text{-}design\text{-}scale}\) is schedule independent because its propensity is a function only of \(E\).  Nonnegativity of all remaining summands therefore gives, for every \(v\in\Delta(\mathcal B)\) and every \(Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,0}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \overline{\mathsf V}_{\mathcal D_n,0}(v)
 &\ge
 8M^2\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1}{n^2}
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}
 \left[
  \frac{1-p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i})}
       {p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i})}
 \right]\\
 &=\frac{8M^2}{n}
 \left\{
  \varepsilon\frac{1-\delta_n}{\delta_n}
  +(1-\varepsilon)
 \right\}\\
 &=8M^2\left\{1+\frac{1-2\varepsilon}{n}\right\}
 \ge 8M^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The equality is precisely the assignment-law weighting of the rare branch described by Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:rare\text{-}history\text{-}stress\text{-}test}\).  Since \(\mathsf B_0(v)\ge0\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:average\text{-}frontier}\) and \(\alpha<1/2\) imply
\[
 \Psi_{\alpha,0}(v)
 \ge \sqrt{\overline{\mathsf V}_{\mathcal D_n,0}(v)/\alpha}
 \ge M\sqrt{8/\alpha}>2M.
\]
This holds for every feasible \(v\), and hence clipping gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M.
\]

It remains to upper-bound the all-kernel minimax length.  Conditional on \(E^c\), define the observable block-\(2\) variables
\[
 X_i=2\mathbf 1\{Z_{2i}=z_1\}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{2i}
     -2\mathbf 1\{Z_{2i}=z_0\}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{2i},
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i.
\]
Both available arms have conditional probability \(1/2\) on \(E^c\).  Sequential randomization thus yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[X_i\mid H_{2i},E^c]
 =Y_{2i}(z_1)-Y_{2i}(z_0)
\]
and, by bounded outcomes,
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[X_i^2\mid H_{2i},E^c]
 =2Y_{2i}(z_1)^2+2Y_{2i}(z_0)^2
 \le4M^2.
\]
Because \(q_2=1\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:target}\) identifies the average of the first display with \(\tau_W\).  Hence
\[
 \Delta_i=X_i-\{Y_{2i}(z_1)-Y_{2i}(z_0)\}
\]
is a martingale difference conditional on \(E^c\).  If \(i<j\), then \(\Delta_i\) is \(H_{2j}\)-measurable and iterated conditioning gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[\Delta_i\Delta_j\mid E^c]
 =\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}
 \left[
  \Delta_i\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[\Delta_j\mid H_{2j},E^c]
  \mathrel{\middle|}E^c
 \right]=0.
\]
The increments are therefore orthogonal.  Since conditional variance is at most the conditional second moment, uniformly over \(Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,0}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}
 [ (\widehat\theta_n-\tau_W)^2\mid E^c]
 =\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}
   \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[\Delta_i^2\mid E^c]
 \le\frac{4M^2}{n}.
\]

Set
\[
 \beta=\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}
       =\frac{\alpha/2}{1-\alpha/2}>0,
 \qquad
 t_n=\frac{2M}{\sqrt{n\beta}}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(t_n<2M\).  Define a deterministic observed-data interval kernel that reports the singleton \(\{0\}\) on \(E\), and on \(E^c\) reports
\[
 J_n=
 [\Pi_M(\widehat\theta_n)-t_n,
   \Pi_M(\widehat\theta_n)+t_n]
 \cap[-2M,2M].
\]
This kernel is schedule independent and always reports a nonempty closed interval because its projected center belongs to \([-2M,2M]\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def:target}\) give \(\tau_W\in[-2M,2M]\).  The metric projection property in Definition \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\) therefore gives
\[
 |\Pi_M(\widehat\theta_n)-\tau_W|
 \le|\widehat\theta_n-\tau_W|.
\]
The pointwise inequality \(\mathbf 1\{|x|>t\}\le x^2/t^2\), valid for \(t>0\), and the preceding second-moment bound imply
\[
 P^O_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(\tau_W\notin J_n\mid E^c)
 \le\frac{4M^2/n}{t_n^2}=\beta.
\]
No coverage is required on the branch \(E\).  Since its probability is \(\varepsilon\) under every schedule,
\[
 P^K_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(\tau_W\in I_K)
 \ge(1-\varepsilon)(1-\beta)=1-\alpha.
\]
Thus the constructed kernel belongs to \(\mathcal C_\alpha\).  Its singleton branch has length zero and \(\operatorname{len}(J_n)\le2t_n\), whence
\[
 \mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star
 \le(1-\varepsilon)2t_n
 =\frac{4M(1-\varepsilon)}{\sqrt{n\beta}}.
\]
Combining this inequality with \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\) gives
\[
 \frac{\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star}
      {\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star}
 \le\frac{2(1-\varepsilon)}{\sqrt{n\beta}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every member of the sequence satisfies all primitive assumptions with \(p_{\min,n}=\varepsilon/n>0\).  A positive comparison constant depending only on \(\alpha\) would contradict the last limit, which proves the proposition.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(0\le\gamma\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\), let \(Y^{(0)}\in\mathcal Y_{M,\gamma}\) be the all-zero fixed schedule.  For any set \(S\subseteq\{(b,i)\in\mathcal T:b\in W\}\), define its target weight and its masked event by
\[
 w(S)=\sum_{(b,i)\in S}\frac{q_b}{n_b},
 \qquad
 E_S=\{Z_{bi}\ne z_1\text{ for every }(b,i)\in S\}.
\]
If the known adaptive design satisfies the computable masked-history reachability condition
\[
 P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^{(0)}}(E_S)\ge1-\eta_\alpha,
\]
then
\[
 \Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\ge2M w(S).
\]
The condition constrains only the total probability of the finite set of zero-outcome assignment histories that avoid the focal arm on \(S\); propensities may otherwise depend arbitrarily on the observed past.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(0\le\gamma\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\).  Define two fixed schedules \(Y^-\) and \(Y^+\) by
\[
 Y^-_{bi}(z_1)=-M,
 \qquad
 Y^+_{bi}(z_1)=M
 \quad ((b,i)\in S),
\]
and set every other available potential outcome, including focal outcomes outside \(S\), equal to zero under both schedules.  All coordinates lie in \([-M,M]\).  Every control block mean is zero, so
\[
 \sum_{b=1}^{B-1}|\mu_{b+1}-\mu_b|=0\le\gamma.
\]
Consequently Definition \(\mathrm{def:schedule\text{-}family}\) gives \(Y^-,Y^+\in\mathcal Y_{M,\gamma}\).  Since the target weights are positive and sum to one, Definition \(\mathrm{def:target}\) gives
\[
 \tau_W(Y^-)=-M w(S),
 \qquad
 \tau_W(Y^+)=M w(S).
\]

We next compare their observed-data laws.  On an assignment prefix containing no focal assignment at a position in \(S\), every observed outcome under \(Y^-\), \(Y^+\), and \(Y^{(0)}\) equals zero.  Starting with the empty history and proceeding in the finite lexicographic order on \(\mathcal T\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization}\) therefore assigns the same conditional probability to every possible next assignment under all three schedules until \(E_S\) is left.  Induction over the enrollment positions yields
\[
 P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^-}(E_S)
 =P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^+}(E_S)
 =P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^{(0)}}(E_S)=:q_S.
\]
The restrictions of \(P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^-}\) and \(P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^+}\) to \(E_S\) also coincide, because both the assignment probabilities and all recorded outcomes coincide along every such history.  On \(E_S^c\), the first focal assignment at a position in \(S\) records outcome \(-M\) under \(Y^-\) and \(M\) under \(Y^+\).  Since \(M>0\), these two sets of full observed records are disjoint.  The common subprobability measure on \(E_S\) has mass \(q_S\), while the two complementary restrictions are mutually singular.  Hence, by the definition of total variation on this finite record space,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}
 \left(P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^-},P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^+}\right)
 =1-q_S
 \le\eta_\alpha.
\]

Take the two priors in Definition \(\mathrm{def:average\text{-}information\text{-}modulus}\) to be the point masses \(\Pi_0=\delta_{Y^-}\) and \(\Pi_1=\delta_{Y^+}\).  They are supported on \(\mathcal Y_{M,\gamma}\), their mixture laws obey the required total-variation bound, and
\[
 \sup_{Y\in\operatorname{supp}(\Pi_0)}\tau_W(Y)+2M w(S)
 =-M w(S)+2M w(S)
 =M w(S)
 =\inf_{Y\in\operatorname{supp}(\Pi_1)}\tau_W(Y).
\]
Thus \(\Delta=2M w(S)\) is feasible in the defining supremum, proving
\[
 \Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\ge2M w(S).
\]
Finally, the reachability probability is directly computable: sum, over the finite assignment paths containing no \(z_1\) at positions in \(S\), the products of the known sequential propensities evaluated at the corresponding zero-outcome histories.  This uses no condition on histories outside that finite masked subtree.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under the primitive sequential-randomization, availability, positivity, boundedness, and control-total-variation conditions, the universally valid comparison is
\[
 \eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)
 \le \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \le 2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
No constant \(c_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) can strengthen the left side to \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) uniformly over this primitive adaptive-design class, even when \(B=3\), \(W=\{2\}\), and \(\Gamma=0\).  A matching radius comparison is recovered on the following structurally restricted but explicitly checkable adaptive subclass.  Let \(Y^{(0)}\) be the all-zero schedule.  Suppose there is a set \(S\subseteq\{(b,i)\in\mathcal T:b\in W\}\) with
\[
 w(S):=\sum_{(b,i)\in S}\frac{q_b}{n_b},
 \qquad
 2M w(S)\ge\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star,
 \qquad
 P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^{(0)}}
 \{Z_{bi}\ne z_1\text{ for every }(b,i)\in S\}
 \ge1-\eta_\alpha.
\]
Then
\[
 \eta_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star
 \le \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \le 2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
The reachability probability is the finite-tree sum of the known sequential path probabilities on zero-outcome histories avoiding \(z_1\) at the positions in \(S\); the design may remain history adaptive away from that subtree.  The choice \(S=\{(b,i):b\in W\}\) has \(w(S)=1\) and therefore gives the simpler sufficient condition that the focal arm is avoided throughout its window with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\).  Coverage and expected length in all displays use the same extended law, and the infimum ranges over every schedule-independent auxiliary-randomized, variable-length observed-data interval kernel.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The uniform lower comparison to the clipped predictable inverse-propensity radius is false when the positive propensity floor may vary across admissible adaptive designs.  The explicit rare-history sequence has radius exactly \(2M\) but minimax expected length tending to zero.  The replacement retains the universally proved mixture-modulus lower bound and factor-two constructive upper bound, states the counterexample, and adds a genuine restricted-design converse derived from a computable masked-history reachability condition rather than assuming a radius-to-modulus comparison.

proposed.justification: The repaired theorem separates what is valid for every known adaptive platform design from the additional finite-tree reachability condition that certifies a matching all-interval converse.
proposed.gap: The unrestricted alpha-only equivalence is refuted by a rare-history design.  Existing Gaussian minimax interval results do not address this assignment-law failure; the proved replacement gives a generic modulus lower bound and a matching radius theorem on an explicitly checkable adaptive masked-history subclass.
proposed.consumer: Trial software may always use the uniformly honest optimized interval and report its factor-two upper guarantee; it may label the radius minimax-equivalent only when the finite adaptive-tree reachability certificate is verified.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim uses two newly proved load-bearing certificates and no longer asserts an alpha-only lower comparison on the unrestricted adaptive-design class, so its dependency and free-symbol metadata must be synchronized.

prose_updates.tldr: A cumulative-discrepancy linear program gives the exact worst-case bias from borrowing nonconcurrent controls, and a finite convex program balances that bias against an assignment-law-averaged predictable-AIPW martingale envelope.  Projection yields an everywhere-nonempty, uniformly design-honest interval with worst-case expected length at most twice the clipped optimized radius.  For every adaptive design, all honest observed-data interval kernels also obey the mixture-modulus lower bound \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\).  An explicit three-block rare-history sequence proves that no positive alpha-only constant can compare this minimax length to the predictable inverse-propensity radius over the unrestricted primitive class: the radius stays at \(2M\) while an honest variable-length interval has expected length tending to zero.  A matching comparison is nevertheless proved on a computable adaptive masked-weight subclass: there must be a set of focal-window positions with target weight \(w\), enough that \(2Mw\) dominates the optimized radius, which the all-zero adaptive tree avoids assigning to the focal arm with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\).  On this class, \(\eta_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\le2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\); avoiding the focal arm throughout the window is a simple sufficient special case.  The KKT borrowing certificate and the accepted boundary results remain distinct: zero drift licenses information-optimal full borrowing, while vacuous drift equates full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel values only under structural invariance of propensities to off-window outcomes.  The separate enumerated one-unit three-block experiment retains its certified zero-drift minimax value \(0.7M\); no positive-drift value is inferred from it.

project_justification.gap: Platform-control papers study parametric or semiparametric calendar adjustment through bias, type-I error, power, or superpopulation efficiency, while Gaussian convex-class work gives minimax expected-length theory in nonadaptive observation experiments.  None supplies a fixed-schedule randomization theorem that distinguishes a universally honest predictable-AIPW upper radius from the smaller expected length achievable by variable-length intervals when severe propensities occur only on rare adaptive histories.  The unrestricted alpha-only equivalence is therefore not merely absent from the literature; it is false.
project_justification.niche: The note treats the adaptive assignment tree itself as part of the experiment.  It combines the exact support function of the bounded-total-variation control-mean class with actual-history martingale information, an all-kernel observed-law mixture modulus, and a finite-tree reachability certificate.  This separates three objects that model-based analyses conflate: the causal finite-population contrast, an implementable honest AIPW radius, and the minimax expected length over all observed-data interval kernels.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution is a sharp bias dual, a convex-program projected interval with worst-case expected length at most twice its clipped radius, a generic all-kernel mixture-modulus lower bound, an explicit rare-history impossibility for any unrestricted alpha-only radius comparison, and a matching radius sandwich on the structurally restricted adaptive subclass having enough target weight on a set of positions whose focal assignments are masked with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\) along the zero-outcome tree.  The existing optimizer certificate characterizes strict gain over the concurrent AIPW rule, and the enumerated one-unit three-block problem retains its exact zero-drift primal--dual value \(0.7M\).  At the endpoints, zero drift removes the borrowing bias, whereas vacuous drift gives equality with the concurrent-only all-kernel benchmark only when propensity updates are structurally unchanged by off-window potential-outcome changes holding assignments and window outcomes fixed.

prose_updates.related_work: LeeWason2020, BofillRoigEtAl2022, and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift analyze all-control versus concurrent-only platform analyses under specified linear, step, fixed-effect, mixed-effect, or spline time models and emphasize bias, type-I error, and power.  MarschnerSchou2024 defines concurrency through randomized cohorts, and SantacatterinaEtAl2025 studies a superpopulation efficiency problem for the concurrent estimand.  Those results motivate the platform setting but do not give uniform fixed-schedule coverage over a total-variation drift class or minimax expected length over schedule-independent observed-data kernels.  LiZhao2026 supplies the predictable-AIPW martingale template; here the assignment law is retained schedule by schedule, so a rare branch contributes through both its probability and its inverse propensity.  ChenLiZhangYe2025, ArmstrongKolesar2018, and CaiLow2004 provide Gaussian bias--variance and mixture-modulus analogies, but their likelihood geometry cannot justify an unrestricted comparison after outcomes feed back into later assignment probabilities.  The present rare-history construction proves that such a comparison is false for the primitive adaptive class.  The positive replacement uses a different, directly verifiable experiment feature: a sufficiently probable zero-outcome subtree on which the focal arm is not reached at a set of positions carrying target weight \(w\).  Two bounded fixed schedules then agree on that subtree and differ by \(2Mw\) in the target, yielding the required total-variation certificate whenever that separation dominates the optimized radius.  AronowLopatto2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 give bounded finite-population minimax benchmarks without staggered availability, bounded calendar drift, or this adaptive-tree obstruction.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The optimized predictable-AIPW radius is a valid constructive upper scale, but it is not the unrestricted minimax expected-length scale.  The counterexample exploits the distinction between a second-moment interval that pays for a rare low-propensity branch and a variable-length procedure that can spend part of its allowed miscoverage on that branch.  The masked-weight reachability condition is sufficient and exactly computable by finite recursion and finite subset search, but it is not claimed necessary and is most relevant when appreciable target weight lies on weakly reached focal positions.  Outside that subclass, the generic lower object remains the observed-law mixture modulus rather than the AIPW radius.  The vacuous-drift reduction separately requires propensity invariance across schedules when only off-window outcomes change; mere predictability does not imply that invariance.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target remains the window-weighted finite-population arm-versus-control contrast, and assignment is the only source of experimental randomness.  The projected AIPW interval is uniformly honest for every design satisfying the primitive support, boundedness, and drift conditions, with no score-consistency or asymptotic-normality assumption.  The all-kernel mixture-modulus lower bound is also generic.  No universal alpha-only equivalence between that interval's optimized radius and minimax expected length is claimed: an explicit admissible three-block sequence refutes it while maintaining a positive propensity floor in every experiment.  Matching constants are asserted only after finding a set of focal-window positions whose target weight \(w\) satisfies \(2Mw\ge\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\) and which the all-zero adaptive tree avoids assigning to the focal arm with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\); the proof constructs the two schedule-supported testing laws explicitly.  Taking the whole window is a simpler sufficient special case.  The KKT result compares NCC and concurrent-only AIPW radii, not the two all-kernel minimax values.  At zero drift, equal control block means remove borrowing bias and permit information-optimal use of all blocks.  At vacuous drift, full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel minimax values coincide only under the accepted structural condition that propensity updates are invariant to off-window potential-outcome changes with assignments and window outcomes fixed.  The separate finite three-block LP asserts only its proved zero-drift value \(0.7M\), supported by matching primal and dual certificates.  No claim is made that the drift budget is identified from trial data, that the masked-weight condition is necessary, or that the finite LP has the same value at positive drift.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem now gives the strongest valid operational statement: a generic factor-two constructive upper bound and mixture-modulus lower bound, an explicit impossibility certificate for unrestricted radius equivalence, and a derived matching sandwich on a finite-tree adaptive reachability subclass.
statement_notes.gap: Gaussian and model-based platform results do not capture the rare-history expected-length obstruction.  The unrestricted comparison is false, while the new masked-history certificate supplies a positive theorem without assuming the crux.
statement_notes.consumer: The NCC implementation can always report the projected uniformly honest interval.  It should advertise minimax equivalence to the optimized radius only after computing and passing the masked-history reachability check; otherwise it should report the generic modulus lower bound and flag rare adaptive branches as a limitation.
